modules.name: Ladybird

sources.x-comment: Ladybird has no tagged releases; this pins to master HEAD as of 2026-09-29. Re-pin periodically.
Matches builtin-baseline in Ladybird's vcpkg.json at the pinned commit above. Must be re-synced whenever the Ladybird git pin above moves.

Prebuilt vcpkg-tool binary, matching VCPKG_TOOL_RELEASE_TAG/VCPKG_GLIBC_SHA in vcpkg/scripts/vcpkg-tool-metadata.txt at the pinned vcpkg commit above. vcpkg.cmake only runs bootstrap-vcpkg.sh (which needs network to fetch this exact file) if $VCPKG_ROOT/vcpkg doesn't already exist -- pre-placing it here skips that network hit entirely. Must be re-synced whenever the vcpkg git pin above moves.
Same as the x86_64 vcpkg-glibc source above, for the aarch64 build (flathub.json only-arches).
flatpak file sources don't preserve/set the executable bit.

Skia bundles libyuv as an external, fetched by vcpkg itself via a raw git clone (no vcpkg_download_distfile hash check). googlesource's +archive endpoint is NOT reproducible across requests (confirmed: two fetches of this exact commit produced two different sha256 hashes), so it can't be a hash-pinned flatpak 'file' source -- a hash-pinned 'git' source (by commit) plus the 'shell' source below (packing it into the .tar.gz vcpkg expects in downloads/) is used instead. Re-sync if the vcpkg git pin above moves.
Same situation as libyuv above: Skia's other googlesource-fetched external.
Same situation as libyuv/piex above, but for the angle port (chromium's zlib fork, one of angle's own third_party deps) rather than skia.

Synthesizes the exact tarballs vcpkg's skia portfile expects to find already cached in downloads/, from the hash-pinned git checkouts above -- no network involved, so this is safe to run in the sandboxed build. Verified: a full (non-download-only) `vcpkg install` against these exact sources, outside the flatpak sandbox but with the sandbox's own VCPKG_ROOT/downloads/ layout, completed successfully for all 69 ports including skia, using tarballs produced this same way.

The ONLY build-time (not source-fetch-time) network dependency found across all 69 vcpkg ports (confirmed by a full local `vcpkg install` run): the angle port's portfile does `pip install ply` inside a venv it creates itself. PIP_NO_INDEX + PIP_FIND_LINKS above (pointed at this dest) make that resolve offline instead. No version was pinned by the portfile itself; this is whatever PyPI currently serves as ply's latest (3.11) -- re-check if angle's portfile ever adds a version constraint.

modules.x-comment: Offline vendoring for vcpkg is believed complete: a full local `vcpkg install` (not just --only-downloads) against the exact sources/config in this module succeeded for all 69 ports, including compiling skia, with the only build-time network need (angle's `pip install ply`) also vendored above. NOT YET verified end-to-end inside the actual flatpak-builder sandbox itself (only outside it, in a distrobox with real network, using the same VCPKG_ROOT/downloads layout) -- that's the next thing to confirm. Rust deps ARE vendored and manifest-verified (see sources/cargo-sources.json). See README.md for full details and what's still open (notably: -DENABLE_QT=ON doesn't appear to pull Qt into the resolved package set).
